tier_reason: First-party vitest bench output (examples/host-typescript/__tests__/example.bench.ts, results in docs/benchmarks.md) with CPU model (AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D) and public build flags (scripts/build-zig.sh, scripts/build-rust.sh), but the Node/V8 version that runs the JS baseline and the wasm, and the Zig/Rust toolchain versions of the run, are not stated, so it falls short of A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Zig: zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast, wasm32-freestanding with +simd128, then wasm-opt -O4 --enable-simd --enable-bulk-memory (scripts/build-zig.sh, examples/wasm-zig/build.zig). Rust (zaw): cargo build --release with opt-level 3, LTO, codegen-units 1, panic=abort, RUSTFLAGS +simd128, then wasm-opt -O4 --enable-simd (scripts/build-rust.sh, examples/wasm-rust/Cargo.toml). wasm-bindgen baseline: wasm-pack build --target web with +simd128. Toolchain versions of the benchmark run not stated: docs/benchmarks.md was last updated 2026-02-17, before the 2026-05-24 'Upgrade to zig 16' commit, so the Zig 0.16.0 badge does not describe the measured build; Rust is unpinned 'stable'; Node/V8 version not stated.
corrections.claimed_speedup: XOR Int32Array (copy in, XOR, read out), zaw Rust build vs plain JavaScript loop: 6.03x at 100 elements, 11.39x at 1,000, 12.80x at 10,000, 13.75x at 100,000; vs Rust wasm-bindgen: 6.20x, 6.88x, 3.32x, 4.32x. zaw Zig build vs JavaScript: 6.0x, 9.7x, 9.9x, 10.0x; vs wasm-bindgen 6.2x, 5.9x, 2.6x, 3.1x (derived from page data). At 10 elements plain JS is 1.66x faster than zaw Rust and 1.67x faster than zaw Zig. Transfer Out Float64Array: zaw 4.3x to 10.65x faster than wasm-bindgen; Transfer In Float64Array: wasm-bindgen 1.03x to 1.22x faster than zaw up to 10,000 elements. 4x4 Float32 matrix multiply: zaw 1.23x (batch 1) to 24.35x (batch 1000) faster than JS.
corrections.caveats: Micro-benchmarks of interop overhead, first-party. Harness asymmetries: the JS XOR baseline allocates a fresh Int32Array per call, while zaw returns a subarray view into the WASM output buffer (implementations/host-typescript/src/conduit.ts readInt32Elements) that the next call overwrites, so a caller that keeps the result must copy it and the 'zero-allocation' gain partly comes from not materializing output; the JS 4x4 matmul baseline does two slice() copies plus a new Float32Array per matrix, which inflates the 20-24x matmul ratios. The wasm-bindgen comparison is fair on kernel (both call the same shared::xor_array_i32), the difference being Vec allocation and copy-out. In 'Transfer In Float64Array' wasm-bindgen is faster than zaw up to 10,000 elements. Toolchain and Node versions of the run are not stated, and the published numbers predate the Zig 0.16 upgrade.

notes: Numbers match docs/benchmarks.md; the record's figures are the zaw Rust build's row (the Zig build is 6-10x vs JS). Kernels really compute the XOR in both zaw builds and the wasm-bindgen baseline; no invalid evidence, but the JS baselines pay per-call typed-array allocation that zaw avoids by returning a reused view. tier_reason: Upgraded from C: harness is public (benchmarks/bench.js, run-one.js, bench-codecs.js, bench-aes.js, run logs in benchmarks/results), runtime (Node.js v26.10.0, Bun 1.4.2, Deno 2.9.7) and CPU (Apple M2) are stated, the measured wasm is the committed binary lib/core/streams/zlib-wasm/zlib-streams.wasm, and its Emscripten build flags are public in the gildas-lormeau/zlib-streams Makefile (-Oz -flto, wasm-opt -Oz). Only the Emscripten version is unstated, which the committed binary makes moot for reproduction; demote to C if a pinned compiler version is required.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Head-to-head (benchmarks/bench.js, fresh Node v26.10.0 process per row, median of 3, level 6): decompress 20 MB text WASM zlib 71 ms vs zip.js pure-JS zlib 155 ms, jszip/pako 140 ms, fflate 116 ms; compress 20 MB incompressible WASM 460 ms vs pure-JS 787 ms, jszip 854 ms (fflate 298 ms is faster); compress 20 MB text WASM 1098 ms vs pure-JS 1229 ms, jszip 1753 ms (fflate 908 ms is faster at 2% larger output); 5,000 x ~2 KB files compress WASM 551 ms vs pure-JS 962 ms, jszip 846 ms (fflate 278 ms is faster). Codec alone (benchmarks/bench-codecs.js, in-process, warm): WASM inflate 41 ms (483.7 MB/s) vs Node DecompressionStream 56 ms, pure-JS 108 ms, fflate 122 ms, i.e. 27% faster than Node's native zlib stream; WASM deflate level 5 493 ms for 6,562,182 bytes vs fflate level 5 534 ms for 6,648,574 bytes; at level 6 WASM 1025 ms is slower than CompressionStream 695 ms. AES-256 WinZip entry, 20 MB stored, write/read (benchmarks/bench-aes.js): WebAssembly 134/135 MB/s vs JavaScript engine 119/108 on Node, 119/121 vs 115/117 on Bun, 124/124 vs 144/133 on Deno (JS faster there); browsers WASM 125/125 vs JS 79/79 (Firefox 156) and 136/138 vs 104/104 (Chrome 153).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: JavaScript baselines and host code on Node.js v26.10.0 (also Bun 1.4.2, Deno 2.9.7; Firefox 156 and Chrome 153 for the browser AES table). The WebAssembly codec is the committed binary lib/core/streams/zlib-wasm/zlib-streams.wasm, built with Emscripten from gildas-lormeau/zlib-streams (madler/zlib submodule plus chunked-inflate, 64-bit compare256 and braided-CRC options): emcc with WASM_CFLAGS -O2 -flto -DDYNAMIC_CRC_TABLE -DBUILDFIXED -DZ_SOLO -DDEFLATE_COMPARE256_64LE -DUSE_ZLIB_RABIN_KARP_ROLLING_HASH -DINFLATE_CHUNK_GENERIC -DINFLATE_CHUNK_READ_64LE, then -Oz -flto -s STANDALONE_WASM=1, then wasm-opt -Oz --enable-bulk-memory-opt (zlib-streams Makefile, target dist/zip-module.wasm). Emscripten version not stated; Makefile read at HEAD, not at the commit that produced the vendored binary.
corrections.caveats: The wasm backend is not the fastest option overall: native CompressionStream and node:zlib beat it on compression (text 678-730 ms vs 1098 ms) and fflate beats it on incompressible data (298 ms) and on small files (278 ms compress, 101 ms decompress); on Node zip.js uses CompressionStream by default at level 6, so the WASM codec runs only for other levels, with useCompressionStream: false, or where no native stream exists. The win is WASM versus the JS port of the same codec and versus pako/fflate, plus a warm inflate 27% faster than Node's DecompressionStream. No decompression row verifies CRC-32 (page says enabling it costs about 7 ms per 20 MB on WASM). Fresh-process rows include about 20 ms of wasm instantiation. Author-run on one Apple M2 machine; levels are not equal work across libraries, which the page handles by printing output sizes. The AES figures in the original record (131 vs 114 MB/s, release 2.15.0 page on jsr.io) are not on BENCHMARKS.md and were replaced with the page's numbers.
